messages.subject: Model testing and parameters
parts:
Hi Nick,

I have two  (unrelated) questions I was hoping you could help me with:

Question 1 - Model testing

I think you talked about this in one of the earlier threads but I am unable to trace it; is it possible to calculate summary statistics to compare a constrained and an unconstrained analysis? For example if I identify DEC+J as the optimum model for my data, is there a way then to compare an unconstrained DEC+J analysis to a constrained one and get AIC weights for them?

Question 2 - Interpreting parameters

(At the risk of sounding like an ignoramus) I am still not sure how to interpret the final values for the parameters. As I understand it, the parameters d, e and j specify the relative probability of dispersal, extinction and founder event speciation at each cladogenetic event (?). If so, why do we have single values for each of these at the end of the run? For example, how would I break down the values d=0.002, e=0; j=0.0391 for readers in the 'Discussion' section of a paper.

Sorry if I am bothering you with something you have already explained and once again, thanks for your time!

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Model testing and parameters
parts: Hi! Thanks for asking on the group...

On Wed, Apr 13, 2016 at 11:32 AM, Utpal Smart <utpal...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Nick,

I have two  (unrelated) questions I was hoping you could help me with:

Question 1 - Model testing

I think you talked about this in one of the earlier threads but I am unable to trace it; is it possible to calculate summary statistics to compare a constrained and an unconstrained analysis? For example if I identify DEC+J as the optimum model for my data, is there a way then to compare an unconstrained DEC+J analysis to a constrained one and get AIC weights for them?

Yes, any model for which you successfully get an ML estimate can be compared to other models using AIC, AICc, etc.  Full discussions:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/advice-on-statistical-model-comparison-in-biogeobears
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#optim


Note that differences in dispersal constraints constitute differences in fixed parameters, not differences in free parameters. This seems to be a common confusion, e.g.:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/mistakes-in-the-literature#examples1

Question 2 - Interpreting parameters

(At the risk of sounding like an ignoramus) I am still not sure how to interpret the final values for the parameters. As I understand it, the parameters d, e and j specify the relative probability of dispersal, extinction and founder event speciation at each cladogenetic event (?). If so, why do we have single values for each of these at the end of the run? For example, how would I break down the values d=0.002, e=0; j=0.0391 for readers in the 'Discussion' section of a paper.

Briefly:

d and e are rates of anagenetic processes that occur on branches.  They are rates per unit time.


The parameter "j" (and the parameters y, s, and v, which are implicitly 1 in Lagrange-DEC, and explicitly 1 in BioGeoBEARS DEC) are *per-event weights*.  At each individual cladogenesis event on the tree, there is a list of possible range inheritance events. Under DEC, each possible event gets a weight of 1.  (probability of a particular event equals weight / (sum of weights).

This was a decision which was hard-coded into Lagrange, and it constitutes a definite statement about the relative probabilities of events at cladogenesis, even though the mechanics of it were not widely known.  BioGeoBEARS lets these weights be modified, e.g. by j, but also potentially in other ways.

The full explanation is here, as well as a discussion of ways to translate to event counts etc. which can be compared.
http://phylo.wikidot.com/per-event-weights-of-cladogenetic-range-inheritance-events-i

Cheers,
Nick
Sorry if I am bothering you with something you have already explained and once again, thanks for your time!
